minutes.headline: Water commissioners voted to adopt the PFAS master plan tying Hickory Hills and Lancaster Ave wells into one treatment plant.
minutes.summary: The board reviewed the engineer's PFAS master plan, the state revolving fund (SRF) financing picture, and litigation funding. It then moved to approve the capital improvement planning summary, with a unanimous vote reported. It also paid a Stantec change order for the Mass Ave water main permit work. Residents pressed for written assurances on Hickory Hills Lake levels during pumping, to be settled before the May 16 vote.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether voting on the plan meant choosing option three; supported it as outside the watershed and cheaper to run one plant.
Asked whether Woodlands residents would be notified of the project via the Hickory Hills board and when that vote would happen.

Raised concern about possible lowering of Hickory Hills Lake level; cited a 1994 DEP approval condition on surface water treatment; asked for binding written assurances and recalled a promised lake-level baseline not carried out.
Raised concern that DEP may restrict chemical weed treatment of the lake and the effect on property values.
public_comment.stated_role: resident and Hickory Hills Landers board member

votes.motion: Approve minutes of March 13th and March 18th
Approve the capital improvement planning summary: Hickory Hills and Lancaster Ave tied via raw water transmission to one treatment facility, plus PFAS treatment for the Keyes well
votes.outcome: passed unanimously (per chair's statement that the board voted unanimously)

votes.motion: Pay Stantec for the Mass Ave water main permit change order

budget_items.what_was_said: The final plan lists Lunenburg for a loan; wording says a low-interest loan with zero percent possible, not guaranteed, and a 20-year standard term.
Conventional bond rates were quoted for 20- and 30-year terms and judged worse than SRF.
The board hopes to raise the SRF request to cover the combined Hickory Hills–Lancaster plant.
A draft comparison showed yearly payments and total interest for a 30-year bond against a zero-percent SRF loan with principal forgiveness, with savings per year.
A minimum is mandatory for small systems and may double, but none is guaranteed.
The district expects some recovery from the suit against the PFAS manufacturers, with no final amount.
Attorneys indicated pilot testing costs might be added to the loan and reimbursed.
A prior fuel-additive suit funded engineering and design for the Keyes well.
The plan totals three well sites: Hickory Hills–Lancaster plant and a separate Keyes treatment plant.

budget_items.topic: Stantec change order, Mass Ave water main
budget_items.what_was_said: Extra engineering for the state permit was approved for payment.
Flowable fill of the old pipe and mill-and-pave of intersections were not in the contract and may be lump-sum cost items.
A prior hydrogeologist option was dropped as an expense.

decisions.decision: Today's vote sets the course of action; a May 16 vote will be on a specific location and amount with updated numbers.
Superintendent to redo the financial comparison at 2% interest and share it for posting.
Board asked the engineer for a written statement of any additional amount written off.
Public sessions set: Apr 4 noon for abutters, Apr 25 6:30 townwide at the high school, May 16 6:30 vote meeting.
Board agreed to pursue written guidelines on lake levels and possibly a mutually agreed third-party hydrogeologist before May 16.

what_happened.line: The Water District board voted to approve a capital improvement planning summary tying the Hickory Hills and Lancaster Ave wells to one treatment facility; the chair said the vote was unanimous.
The board also approved paying Stantec a change order for extra engineering on the Mass Ave water main state permit; the recorded vote was not audible.
The chair said today's vote sets a course of action, and a May 16 vote will be on a specific location and amount with updated numbers.
The board reviewed state revolving fund (SRF) financing against a conventional bond, and the superintendent was asked to redo the comparison at a 2% rate for posting.
After residents raised Hickory Hills Lake levels, the board agreed to seek written guidelines and possibly a shared third-party hydrogeologist before May 16.

why_it_matters: The PFAS plan sets which treatment plant design the district pursues, and the loan terms behind it affect what water customers may later be asked to pay.
The SRF loan wording says a zero percent rate and principal forgiveness are possible but not guaranteed, so the financing figures shown so far are not settled.
Residents will be asked to vote on May 16 on a specific site and amount, and lake-level assurances for Hickory Hills are meant to be settled before then.
